suggestions.suggestion: The new bracketing assertion in Test_processData_versionChange_recomputesLayout, `assert.Less(t, strings.Index(normalized, "olddb"), hdrPos, ...)`, passes vacuously if "olddb" is absent, since strings.Index returns -1 and -1 < hdrPos. It is not a real hole — the earlier `assert.Contains(t, normalized, "olddb")` catches that case — but the failure output would then show the Contains failure plus a silently-passing ordering check. Promoting that Contains to require.Contains, or capturing `oldPos := strings.Index(...)` with a `require.NotEqual(t, -1, oldPos)` alongside the existing hdrPos/rowPos guards, makes the bracket self-sufficient and matches the pattern the same test already uses two lines above.
suggestions.benefit: The new assertion carries its own precondition rather than borrowing one from an assert further up, consistent with how hdrPos and rowPos are already guarded.
